A call center manager thinks the number of calls to the center per minute has increased since they started offering a new service. Before the new service was offered, the average number of calls per minute was $6$. Let $X$ represent the number of calls arriving at the call center during a one-minute period. Under the null hypothesis that the number of calls is the same as before, what is the critical region of a one-tailed test at a significance level of $2%$?

*Hint: You may use the table below, representing the **cumulative distribution function** of $X$ under the null hypothesis.*

| $x$ | $⋯$ | $9$ | $10$ | $11$ | $12$ | $13$ | $⋯$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P(X \le x)$ | $⋯$ | $0.9161$ | $0.9574$ | $0.9799$ | $0.9912$ | $0.9964$ | $⋯$ |

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.

Mary owns a pastry shop and believes her new muffin recipe will increase muffin sales. With the previous recipe, an average of $4$ out of $10$ customers bought at least one muffin. Let $X$ represent the number of customers buying at least one new muffin in a random sample of $8$. Under the null hypothesis that the proportion of customers that buy a muffin with the new recipe is the same as before, what is the critical region of a one-tailed test at a significance level of $2.5%$?

*Hint: You may use the table below, representing the **cumulative distribution function** of $X$ under the null hypothesis.*

| $x$ | $⋯$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ | $8$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P(X \le x)$ | $⋯$ | $0.5941$ | $0.8263$ | $0.9502$ | $0.9915$ | $0.9993$ | $1.0000$ |

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
